Title: ​Aga Khan University Hospital is ISO 9002 certified - a First in Pakistan
NewsSummary: ​The Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH) has become the first teaching hospital in Pakistan to be ISO 9002 certified.
NewsContent:
​The Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH) has become the first teaching hospital in Pakistan to be ISO 9002 certified. It now has the singular distinction of being one of the first few teaching hospitals in the world to receive this prestigious certification.

The ISO journey began in August 1997. In April 1999, six AKUH departments received the ISO 9002 certification. A decision was then taken to have the entire Hospital certified in the year 2000. A team of five auditors from AIB-Vincotte International Limited of Belgium carried out the final two-day audit. The audit team checked compliance with the documented systems, their implementation and overall effectiveness. The auditors were impressed with AKUH's level of compliance to the ISO 9002 Quality Management System, and announced that the Hospital would be recommended for ISO 9002 certification, which it has now received.

Commenting on this achievement, Mr. John B. Stevens, Director of University Administration and Director General of the Hospital said, "It has been a major challenge, involving over 3,000 faculty and staff, whose unflinching dedication has ensured a new milestone in this University's history."

AKUH is the integrated healthcare delivery unit of the Aga Khan University. It seeks to provide exemplary care while remaining accessible to all patients. More than 70 per cent of the nearly 350,000 patients who visit the Hospital every year are from low and middle-income households. Care is provided through a broad range of secondary and tertiary services, supported by professional staff with facilities that are amongst the best in the region. The ISO 9002 certification further ensures compliance to the highest standards of patient care that the Hospital has set for itself.
